title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met on Monday afternoon and took little time navigating through a very light agenda.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and those gather recited the Pledge of Allegiance and Commissioners Phil Wiley offered the prayer.

The mayor opened the floor to visitors and recognized Nikki Green with the Flora Community Market.  Green noted that with the changing of the seasons quickly approaching, they are planning for a Flora Community Market Harvest Fest to close out the year on Saturday, October 24 starting at 8:00am and staying open until 2:00pm that final day with Main St. closed from 2nd to 3rd Streets.  Commissioners approved her request unanimously.

With no representative for the Flora Coon Club, the council tabled there scheduling request and moved on.

Next, Jacob Martin representing Clay City High School, Sarah Hudson from Flora High School and Sam Erwin from North Clay are interested in teaming up for a co-op cross-country meet at Charley Brown Park on Monday and Tuesday, October 19 and 20.  Martin shared the route within the park and noted they would need some help with marking the course and implementing road closures to allow for the safety of the participating athletes.  All three agreed that Charley Brown Park is an excellent venue for running events with Mayor Spicer acknowledging that she was a little surprised it isn’t used more often for cross-country meets.  Commissioner Jim Fehrenbacher stated he remembers events from his high school days at Charley Brown Park.  Mayor Spicer clarified that Clay City is the main organizer for the meet and reminded Martin that they would have to provide proof of insurance and he was aware of the requirement.  A motion was made to approve the event and was approved without dissent.

Commissioners next approved the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included the past meeting minutes, the police activity report for August as well as the building and zoning report, the Treasurer’s report and the warrant list for the last half of August.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer thanked everyone for their work during the Ford Town Fun Fest this past weekend and the Tourism Committee who put it on, as well as the public who attended.  She also reminds everyone that this is homecoming week at Flora High School with the parade through the downtown area Wednesday, the bonfire later that night and the football game Friday night and the homecoming coronation and dance on Saturday night.  Before moving on, the mayor, with commissioners consent, re-appointed Lacey Lewis to a two-year term on the Flora Tourism Committee that expires September 21, 2028.

When the mayor polled the council for their comments, Commissioner Jeremy Henderson asked again about the status of the downtown grants for which the city has applied. Mike Stanford told they heard back today and they asked four additional questions, which he quasi-joked that that’s fewer than before and perhaps next time it will be down to two questions.  Other than that he didn’t have any additional update about the grant status.  Commissioner Phil Wiley used his time to praise this past weekend’s Ford Town Fun Fest activities.  While he noted there were fewer car show entries and a smaller crowd, he and others who attended believed it all boiled down to the heat.  But for those who braved the conditions, a good time was had by all with Wiley especially impressed by the music Friday evening.  He thanked the vendors, the contestants for the chili cookoff and the craft brewers competition and everyone who came out and said it was a great event.

Flora City Administrator and Economic Development Director Mike Stanford presented one item for consideration.  The measure was an annexation ordinance for the property at 66 Red Bay Lane owned by Anthony Casolari.  After some clarification that the property is a vacant lot, the ordinance was adopted unanimously.  Stanford closed out his time by noting that at the next meeting they’ll go over road maintenance for the city.  He said they have opened the bids received and they came in about $40,000 below the estimate.

title: APPLEKNOCKER 26
full_story:
The Flora Academic Foundation Appleknocker will be held on Saturday from 9:30 to 2:30 pm at the Flora Elementary School.  There will be free entertainment, great food and fun and games for all ages.

Activities will begin at 9:30 with flag raising ceremonies with the Shooting Stars Drill Team.  The Flora High School Band under the direction of Ethan Steber, will perform at 9:45 followed by DAS-zle Dance and Tumble at 10:30 pm in the FES multipurpose room.  From 11 to 1 a youth open mic hosted by Matt Lovett will take place on the outside stage.  Power and Grace Tumbling and Dance will perform at 1 pm inside the FES multipurpose room.

Food and Games will be onsite all day, the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders will have a pedal tractor pull and Clay County emergency vehicles will be available for tours, and there will be a hands-on robotics display.  Parking will be available at the Football Field.  The festival will close at 2:30 pm.

The Flora Academic Foundation provides financial support to supplement, enrich, and enhance quality programs and educational opportunities for the children of the Flora Unit School District.  Visit the FAF/Appleknocker link on the flora school website for more information.

title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The Flora School Board met in regular session last night approving the 26-27 budget and a number of school trips.

The board opened the meeting with a public hearing on the 26-27 budget and later adopted the budget.  They also approved the administrative and teacher salary reports, and the bid for roof work at Flora High School submitted by D7 Roofing.

Superintendent Joel Hackney highlighted the upcoming Appleknocker and the end of the first quarter.  He also discussed district goals with the areas of curriculum, building and grounds, safety, communication, and extracurricular activities emphasized.

In personnel action the board approved Landon Carder as JH golf coach and Taylor Jones and Jamie Vanscyoc as volunteer assistant coaches for junior high golf for the 2027 season.  They accepted the resignation as 6th grade boys’ basketball coach effective September 1st, submitted by Marty Hustad.  The Board acknowledged the receipt of FMLA leave for Rheyse Kimmell from December 21st through March 31st and the FMA leave for Ethan Steber from January 4th through January 29th.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Police Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for August during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated 12 traffic accidents.

They made five criminal arrests.  There were three drug arrests and one DUI arrest during August.  There were two local ordinance arrests, 12 traffic arrests and six warrant arrests.

Officers issued 39 warning tickets, responded to 17 alarms and had 1,194 calls for service and had two juvenile contacts.

Also, Flora police officers drove 4,957 miles and conducted 82 investigations during August.  They answered 308, 911 calls and conducted 15 UTV Inspections and no Golf Cart Inspections during August.

title: CHILD SAFETY SEAT INSPECTIONS
full_story:
On Friday, the Clay County Health Department will be offering Car Seat Safety checks from Noon until 4 pm.

During this time certified child passenger safety technicians will provide a free car seat safety check.  Is your car seat expired, installed correctly or is it the right seat for your child.  Find out for free and get any questions answered.

This is Illinois Child Passenger Safety Week and parents and caregivers are reminded that state law requires children to ride in a child safety seat until age 8 and rear-facing until age 2.  During this time certified child passenger safety technicians provide free car seat safety checks throughout the state as part of Child Passenger Safety Week.

According to statistics 3 out of every 4 Child Safety Seats are installed incorrectly.

title: FLORA BUILDING AND ZONING REPORT
full_story:
Flora Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented the monthly building and zoning report for August during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

The report shows four new residential construction projects were undertaken in August, valued at $75,819.

There were six new commercial projects started during August, valued at $313,000.

And there were no new industrial projects started during August.

There was a total of ten new projects in Flora, valued at $388,819 with $1,370 collected in permit fees and $500 in deposit fees collected for August.

The year-to-date figures show 45 total residential projects so far this year with a value of $667,439.

There are ten year-to-date commercial projects valued at $17,757,334 and no new industrial projects for the year.

That makes 55 total projects valued at $18,424,773, with $3,743 in permit fees and $1,100 in deposit fees collected for the year.

title: KINMUNDY LOG CABIN VILLAGE
full_story:
The annual Fall Festival at the Kinmundy Log Cabin Village is coming up, Saturday and Sunday, at the Kinmundy Log Cabin Village on Gesell Road.  The Fall Festival offers visitors a chance to step back in time while enjoying a full weekend of family fun.

Admission is five dollars, with children five and under admitted free.  Festival hours are 10 am to 5 pm on Saturday and 10 am to 4 pm on Sunday.

The event features more than 150 craft and food vendors, along with live demonstrations and plenty of activities for the entire family.  Visitors can also explore the village’s collection of historic 1800s log cabins while enjoying the sights, sounds and flavors of the fall season.

The Kinmundy Log Cabin Village is located at 6260 Gesell Road in Kinmundy. For more information, visit kinmundylogcabinvillage.com.
